comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Reproduced the reported failure LOCALLY and deterministically before fixing it. From a cold tests/e2e/js (node_modules + dist removed), `pytest tests/e2e -n 4 --dist worksteal` produced exactly the CI signature: `[gw3] node down: Not properly terminated` / `[gw1] node down: Not properly terminated`, 2 failed / 12 passed / 7 skipped in 306.60s. That run already carried an explicit per-step timeout and an flock, which is the finding worth recording: a lock ALONE does not fix this. Under -n 4 every worker runs the session-scoped fixture, so serializing them converts the race into a QUEUE that is still charged to a test's 300s pytest-timeout budget — the waiters were killed instead of the installer.

The fix therefore moves provisioning out of the fixture into `pytest_collection_modifyitems` in tests/e2e/conftest.py. Collection is not a test item, so pytest-timeout does not bound it; the fixture keeps a last-resort fallback that re-reports rather than re-runs a failed provisioning.

Post-fix, same cold state, no pre-step: 21 passed in 111.83s, no worker kill. With `make e2e-deps` run first: 21 passed in 71.80s and the slowest single span is 7.57s (was 90-120s of fixture setup billed to one test). `make e2e-deps` itself took 7m02s cold on this host — which is precisely why it must not sit inside a test's budget.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
RCA confirmed (2026-09-03): `tests/e2e/test_editor_e2e.py::test_emitted_bpmn_has_no_illegal_ids` worker crashes are a pre-existing test/toolchain flake, not caused by `8eff-87c1-d09a-4893` / Gerrit 2592.

Evidence:
- CI crash fingerprint recurred twice on Gerrit 2592: run 33815705743 py3.13 logged `[gw0] node down: Not properly terminated`, then `worker 'gw0' crashed while running 'tests/e2e/test_editor_e2e.py::test_emitted_bpmn_has_no_illegal_ids'`, with coverage reporting a failed worker and no test assertion; run 33819616393 py3.11 logged the same node-down/crashed-worker signature.
- Current `origin/main` reproduction worktree: `85ef5ad33ada9540d18bd17775bf2a521ef6ccbb` (= `origin/main`). The e2e fixture does lazy Node provisioning in test setup: `tests/e2e/conftest.py:47-58` runs `npm install` / `npm run build` inside session-scoped `bpmn_harness` when `node_modules` or `dist/roundtrip.mjs` is absent. Pytest's global timeout covers fixture setup (`pyproject.toml:719-720`, `timeout=300`, `timeout_method=thread`), and CI runs the default tier under xdist worksteal (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:781-786`). The workflow comments document the failure mode: the thread timeout exits the worker, producing `node down: Not properly terminated` instead of a normal timeout failure (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:772-777`).
- Discriminating local experiments: cold toolchain + isolation with the normal 300s budget timed out in fixture setup after 300s while blocked in `subprocess.run([npm, "install"], cwd=_JS_DIR, ...)` (`tests/e2e/conftest.py:51-53`). Cold toolchain + xdist + deliberately-short `--timeout=10 --timeout-method=thread` reproduced the exact xdist crash signature: `[gw3] node down: Not properly terminated` and `worker 'gw3' crashed while running ...test_emitted_bpmn_has_no_illegal_ids` in 11.38s. With the toolchain preinstalled and bundle prebuilt, the same xdist command with `--timeout=10` passed in 1.50s. This rules out BPMN illegal-id assertion failure, BPMN serialization nondeterminism, and 8eff docs/scripts changes; the crash is caused by provisioning work happening inside the per-test timeout window.
- 8eff/Gerrit 2592 patchset 2 only changes docs/ADR/API-stability/architecture and script-policy tests: `docs/adr/.numbers/0111`, `docs/adr/0111-no-internal-only-compatibility-shims.md`, `docs/adr/README.md`, `docs/api-stability.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `tests/scripts/test_internal_shim_policy_docs.py`, `tests/scripts/test_no_internal_shim_policy.py`. It does not touch `tests/e2e/`, BPMN/editor code, Node harness code, pytest timeout config, or CI xdist command lines.

Classification: (a) genuine pre-existing flaky/test-isolation/resource-timeout bug independent of 8eff. Not a provably transient infra-only fault: the class is reproducible locally by constraining the same pytest-timeout mechanism, and CI hit it on two interpreter shards. Defect origin: ticket `bold-abeyant-indri` (`73b8-2d79-3046-44ce`), commit `6a5c88027c59d3e24d3e4269838fb3c591a64240` (`Adopt standard test-hygiene tooling`) introduced the global fixture-covering pytest-timeout mechanism; the pre-existing lazy e2e provisioning then became capable of killing xdist workers when registry/install latency exceeded the budget.

Minimal fix required: move e2e Node provisioning out of the `bpmn_harness` fixture/test timeout budget (prefer CI/local `make e2e-deps` using lockfile-based `npm ci` before pytest, plus a collection/session-level fallback that is not charged to an individual test item), and keep any fallback subprocesses explicitly bounded/diagnostic. Do not unblock 8eff with a blind `recheck`; either land this class fix first, or accept a targeted recheck only as a tactical retry with known residual flake risk, not because the evidence proves transient infra.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PRIORITY RAISED TO 0. New evidence: this defect is currently failing ~46% of ALL CI runs repo-wide, not just the changes that first surfaced it. Over the last 60 Gerrit Verified runs (2026-09-03 14:27Z to 09-04 03:01Z): 27 success, 23 failure of 50 completed. It blocks every open change in the repository.

IT IS NOT INTERMITTENT, AND THAT CORRECTS HOW I FRAMED IT. I posted a recheck on change 2594 describing this as an 'intermittent race'. That was wrong. It is a FIXED, UNBOUNDED-COST fixture measured against a FIXED budget, and the cost has grown until it straddles the 300s cliff. Measured setup times for test_emitted_bpmn_has_no_illegal_ids on jobs that PASSED, from --durations output:
  40.96s  (run 33815025971, py3.11)
  101.86s (run 33829699178, py3.12)
  201.58s (run 33829352524, py3.12)
  271.35s (run 33819649550, py3.12)  <- 90% of the 300s budget, barely passed
Anything over 300s trips timeout_method='thread', which calls os._exit(1) and kills the worker. So which matrix cells fail varies run to run while the underlying cost does not -- that is why a recheck did not clear it and why it lands on different Python versions each time. Corroboration that it is a timeout and not OOM or a segfault: no [rebar-ci-timing] warning for bpmn_harness appears in ANY failing log, because the fixture never completed setup.

ONSET IS SHARP: last fully clean run 33811108275 at 2026-09-03T22:02:43Z; first gw0 crash run 33813339060 at 22:30:05Z; zero occurrences from 09-03 01:04Z through 22:02Z. No commit merged in that window touches the e2e/Node/CI path.

THREE THINGS THE FIX MUST ACCOUNT FOR:

1. PLAYWRIGHT DOMINATES THE COLD INSTALL and is a devDependency needed only by browser_runner, not by bpmn_harness. Removing it from the bpmn_harness provisioning path is the single cheapest lever and may alone drop the cost below the cliff. Evaluate this even if the structural fix lands too.

2. THE VERIFIED LANE RUNS WORKFLOWS FROM TRUSTED MAIN, so a CI-side pre-provisioning step CANNOT be validated from a patchset -- it only takes effect once merged. Plan for that: do not expect a green Verified on the patchset that introduces the CI step, and do not read its absence as failure.

3. THE PORTABLE HALF IS STILL REQUIRED. A CI-only pre-provision step does not satisfy project.portability. The in-process path must also work with no CI provider -- either provisioning outside any test's budget (a pytest_sessionstart or collection hook) or an explicit marked timeout naming the provisioning cost.

macOS never exercises this: DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS restricts the macOS job to platform_compat, and test_editor_e2e appears zero times in the macOS log. So the matrix hides the defect on one of four cells.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Patchset 2 pushed (change 2600). Remediation of LLM-Review -1 + Verified -1, plus the P0 escalation.

Verified -1 was MINE, not a pre-existing flake: tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py::test_completeness_every_gate_step_is_guarded_or_marked. The Verified lane runs workflows from trusted main against an arbitrary patchset, so a base predating this change has no e2e-deps rule and a bare 'make e2e-deps' would have failed the step — turning this fix into a red vote on other people's changes. Now guarded with a 'make -n e2e-deps' probe. Worth recording the local/CI skew that hid it: the gate only considers git-TRACKED paths, so my local run passed while tests/e2e/_toolchain.py was still untracked and CI failed the moment it was committed.

LLM-Review blocking finding (the collection hook had no oracle) is addressed by driving the REAL conftest through a nested pytest over a replica tree with stub node/npm. Coverage is mutation-checked: eight mutations, all killed. One test was found VACUOUS by that exercise — removing the _PROVISION_ATTEMPTED guard changed nothing observable, because pytest_collection_modifyitems fires once per session. The flag was dead mechanism, so it was deleted rather than papered over with a test; _PROVISION_ERROR alone carries every observable behaviour.

Advisory 1 was a real bug and is fixed: browser_runner never consulted the provisioning state, so a failed npm ci surfaced for bpmn_harness and not for it.

Escalation lever (playwright): measured, and the wall-clock number is NOT usable from this host — paired cold runs gave 111.8s omit-optional vs 63.4s full, then 420.9s omit-optional, i.e. registry variance dominates; --offline with a warm cache is ~1s either way. The reliable measurements are counts and bytes: 15 -> 11 packages, 30M -> 12M node_modules (playwright 4.8M + playwright-core 12M = 56% of the tree). One correction to the escalation: the published playwright package has NO postinstall script, so there is no browser download in this path — the saving is package download/extract only. playwright is now an optionalDependency and a selection with no browser test installs with --omit=optional.

Note for readers of the next Verified run: the CI-side pre-provisioning step CANNOT be exercised on this patchset, because the Verified lane runs the workflow from trusted main. Only the portable in-process half is under test here.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Patchset 2 up on change 2600. Three corrections and one measurement worth pinning, including one to my own escalation comment above.

CORRECTION TO MY ESCALATION -- the playwright lever is real but smaller than implied. I relayed it as 'dominates the cold install'. Measured properly it dominates in BYTES, not because of a browser download: the published playwright package has NO postinstall script (verified in its package.json: scripts: None), so nothing downloads browsers on this path. The saving is package download and extract only. The honest numbers:
  full npm ci             : 15 packages, 30M node_modules
  npm ci --omit=optional  : 11 packages, 12M node_modules
  playwright 4.8M + playwright-core 12M = 16.8M = 56% of the tree
On a cold-cache runner that is still the dominant download fraction, so the lever was worth taking -- it is now an optionalDependency with --omit=optional for selections containing no browser test. But 'playwright downloads browsers' would have been wrong and is deliberately not in the commit message.

WALL-CLOCK MEASUREMENT IS NOT OBTAINABLE FROM THIS HOST, which is itself worth recording so nobody retries it. Paired cold runs: --omit=optional 111.8s, full 63.4s, then --omit=optional again 420.9s. Registry variance dominates and INVERTS the comparison. Against a warm cache with --offline it is ~1s either way. Counts and bytes are the only stable evidence here.

THE VERIFIED -1 ON PATCHSET 1 WAS OURS, NOT THE PRE-EXISTING FLAKE, and the substance is worse than the message. test_predates_gate_guard_parity flagged an unguarded 'make e2e-deps' in the workflow. Because the Verified lane runs workflows from TRUSTED MAIN against an arbitrary patchset, a base predating this change has no e2e-deps rule, so the bare invocation fails the step -- this fix for a repo-wide CI failure would itself have cast red votes on everyone else's changes. Now guarded with a 'make -n e2e-deps' probe (which also keeps the guard reading the tree's own Makefile, the only thing that can answer the question) plus an ::notice:: on the skip path.

LOCAL/CI SKEW THAT HID IT, worth knowing generally: that gate considers only GIT-TRACKED paths. A 16718-passing local run was green while tests/e2e/_toolchain.py was still untracked, and CI failed the instant it was committed. Re-running the gate after 'git add' is the habit that catches this class.

A VACUOUS TEST WAS FOUND AND THE MECHANISM DELETED RATHER THAN PROTECTED. Removing 'if _PROVISION_ATTEMPTED: return' from the hook changed nothing observable, because pytest_collection_modifyitems fires once per session -- it was dead mechanism. The right response was deleting the flag, not writing a test to defend it. _PROVISION_ERROR alone now carries every observable behaviour and every remaining branch has a killing mutation. Eight mutations applied, all eight killed.

STRONGEST EVIDENCE IN THE CHANGE: cold state (node_modules and dist removed), CI xdist config, no pre-step -> 63 passed in 442.35s with NO worker kill. On the old code the identical cold state killed two workers at the 300s cliff (2 failed, 12 passed, 7 skipped in 306.60s). 442s of wall clock, none of it charged to any test's budget.

REMINDER FOR REVIEWERS: a still-red Verified on this patchset is EXPECTED and is not evidence the CI step is wrong. The Verified lane runs workflows from trusted main, so the pre-provisioning step and the npm cache cannot take effect until this merges. Only the portable in-process half is under test on the patchset -- which is why that half carries the mutation-checked coverage.

comments.body:
CONFIRMED: THIS DEFECT FAILS ON MAIN ITSELF, not only on patchsets. The last scheduled branch-head run of test.yml (33824556786, 2026-09-04T01:07:53, schedule trigger on main) failed on 'build-and-test / pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.13)' and 'sweep (windows)'. So main's own health signal is red from this bug, independently of anything in review. Branch health therefore comes from the schedule, meaning a defect like this one degrades main's health signal for up to ~6 hours before it is even visible.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Patchset 3 pushed (change 2600), rebased onto origin/main 6125c5345f01 — merge-base is now main's head and rev-list HEAD..origin/main is 0, so the Gerrit merge conflict is cleared. One conflict during the rebase, in the Makefile .PHONY line: main added 'scanner-integration' while this change added 'e2e-deps'; resolved by keeping both.

Blocking finding taken, and taken as a DESIGN rule rather than a second patch. This change's CI wiring has now risked breaking other people's builds twice — first the unguarded 'make e2e-deps' that test_predates_gate_guard_parity caught, now its intolerance of a transient npm failure. Both have the same shape: pre-provisioning is an OPTIMISATION, so its failure must degrade to the in-fixture path, never fail the step. The step now has three explicit skip paths (macOS lane, no e2e-deps rule on this tree, provisioning failed), each emitting a ::notice:: so a silent skip cannot read as success. The Makefile target stays STRICT — a developer running it wants to be told the install failed — and CI tolerates its failure instead of the target pretending to succeed.

Advisories taken: (a) the collection hook could leak a non-ToolchainProvisioningError — an OSError from the lock mkdir/open/flock would have aborted COLLECTION itself, taking down tests unrelated to the e2e tier; every failure is now converted to the named error kind. (b) the node/npm guard on 'make e2e-deps' had no test; it now has one that runs the target with a PATH containing only 'make' and asserts exit 0 plus the skip message.

Advisories declined, with reasons: pinning Node to an exact patch version (a yanked patch release then breaks CI, and the lockfile — not the Node patch level — determines what is built); making 'make e2e-deps' omit the browser stack (a pre-pytest step does not yet know the selection, and CI runs the browser tier); dropping the lockfile hash from restore-keys (that is what a restore-key prefix is FOR, and ~/.npm is content-addressed, so a superset cache is beneficial rather than unsafe).

Three new mutation checks, all killed: CI invoking 'make e2e-deps' unguarded; a lock failure escaping as a raw OSError; the Makefile losing its node guard. Eleven mutations killed across the change now.

Separately: the scanner-integration Verified failure on patchset 2 is NOT this ticket. 'python: can't open file .../scripts/install_review_scanners.py' — that file arrived in 6125c5345f01 and .github/workflows/_scanner-integration.yml is absent from GUARDED_WORKFLOWS in tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py, so the gate that exists to catch exactly this class does not cover the new workflow. Tracked as 90c7-c465-4037-42d5; not touched here.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
MERGED. Change 2600 landed as 668523feffde on Gerrit main with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 (the GitHub mirror was still catching up at the time of writing).

Residual, deliberately not folded in so the priority-0 unblocker could land: provision_toolchain still evaluates _satisfied() BEFORE taking the flock, and treats the bundle as ready on mere existence, so a worker can return early and run a bundle another worker is still writing. Filed as chiselled-thrifty-gnat (477b-4130-424d-41eb), linked discovered_from this bug, with the fix (check inside the lock) and a RED-first concurrency oracle already scoped.

Three other LLM-Review advisories were declined with reasons recorded on the change: pinning Node to an exact patch version, making the portable target omit the browser stack, and dropping the lockfile hash from the npm cache restore-keys. A fourth — no workflow step runs 'npx playwright install chromium' — is pre-existing behaviour that this change did not alter (browser_runner already self-skips when Chromium is unavailable); noted here rather than filed, since it predates this work.

Ticket left in_progress for the orchestrator to close.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA VERIFIED AGAINST MERGED MAIN (668523feffde), not against the agent's report. Change 2600 is MERGED with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

AC1 -- explicit timeouts and a named failure. tests/e2e/_toolchain.py:103 passes timeout=timeout to the subprocess; ToolchainProvisioningError is defined at :63; the message at :111 reads 'e2e toolchain: `{label}` timed out after {timeout:g}s in {cwd}', so the failing STEP is named rather than the worker being killed anonymously.

AC2 -- portable pre-pytest provisioning. Makefile:470 defines e2e-deps. This is the no-CI-provider trigger required by project.portability; CI merely invokes it, and the in-fixture path remains as fallback.

AC3 -- cache and npm ci. .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:474 keys the cache on
${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ steps.e2e-node.outputs.node-version }}-${{ hashFiles('tests/e2e/js/package-lock.json') }} -- note it also includes the NODE VERSION, closing an advisory that a Node upgrade could reuse a cache built by a different toolchain. Makefile:493 runs 'npm ci'; _toolchain.py:160 documents npm install as the fallback for a tree with no lockfile.

AC4 -- concurrent provisioning serialized. _toolchain.py:86 takes fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX), released at :94, around install+build, with a documented degradation where fcntl is absent (:27).

AC5 -- verified in real time, deterministically, not by waiting for a recurrence. Cold state with node_modules and dist removed, under the CI xdist configuration: 31 passed, NO worker kill. The identical cold state on the old code killed two workers at the 300s cliff (2 failed, 12 passed, 7 skipped in 306.60s). Separately, stalling npm past the new bound yields the named AC1 failure rather than 'node down'.

THE FIX SHAPE CHANGED DURING IMPLEMENTATION, AND THE REASON IS WORTH KEEPING: a lock alone does NOT fix this. The first implementation was exactly what this ticket described -- explicit timeouts plus a lock, provisioning still inside the fixture -- and it STILL REPRODUCED, because under -n 4 --dist worksteal every worker runs the session fixture, so serialising them converts the race into a QUEUE that is still charged to a test's budget: the waiters get killed instead of the installer. Only moving provisioning out of the fixture into pytest_collection_modifyitems fixes it, because collection is not a test item and pytest-timeout does not bound it.

Eleven mutations killed across the change. One test was found VACUOUS by that exercise -- deleting _PROVISION_ATTEMPTED changed nothing observable, since the hook fires once per session -- and the dead mechanism was deleted rather than protected by a new test.

Also taken: playwright moved to optionalDependencies (16.8M of a 30M tree, 15 packages -> 11 with --omit=optional). Correcting my own earlier framing: playwright has NO postinstall script, so nothing downloads browsers here; the saving is package download and extract only.

Follow-up filed, deliberately not folded in: 477b-4130-424d-41eb (chiselled-thrifty-gnat) -- provision_toolchain still evaluates _satisfied() BEFORE the flock, so a worker can run a bundle another is still writing. Not a regression: before this change there was no lock at all. Landing the P0 unblocker was judged worth more than resetting a green +1.

Noted but not filed, pre-existing and untouched: no workflow step runs 'npx playwright install chromium', so browser_runner self-skips on 'Chromium unavailable' in CI -- an entire test tier silently skipping.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`tests/e2e/test_editor_e2e.py::test_emitted_bpmn_has_no_illegal_ids` intermittently fails in CI
as `worker 'gw0' crashed` / `[gw0] node down: Not properly terminated`, with no traceback and no
assertion — a killed xdist worker, not a test failure. Observed on unrelated Gerrit changes 2592,
2593 and 2594 within ~30 minutes on 2026-09-03. It costs every contributor a red `Verified` vote
on work that is not at fault, and AGENTS.md forbids retrying a flake instead of root-causing it.

## Root cause (measured, confirmed in the tree)

`tests/e2e/conftest.py::bpmn_harness` is session-scoped and provisions the Node toolchain lazily
inside the FIRST e2e test's setup: `subprocess.run([npm, "install"], …)` at
`tests/e2e/conftest.py:52` and `subprocess.run([npm, "run", "build"], …)` at
`tests/e2e/conftest.py:58`. Neither carries a `timeout=`, unlike every other subprocess in the
same file (`:74` `timeout=60`, `:118` `timeout=150`), so their only bound is the global
pytest-timeout: `timeout = 300` / `timeout_method = "thread"` at `pyproject.toml:719-720`,
deliberately without `timeout_func_only`, so the budget covers fixture setup. The `thread`
method calls `os._exit(1)` — documented in-tree at
`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:774` — so an over-run kills the whole worker instead of
reporting `Failed: Timeout`. In passing CI run 33811108275 that setup is the slowest span in the
suite (101.26s / 120.93s / 89.69s across py3.11/3.12/3.13); 90-120s of a 300s budget is a
2.5-3.3x margin that npm-registry variance can consume. There is no `setup-node` step and no npm
cache in `.github/workflows/`, so every run pays a cold registry install, and under
`-n 4 --dist worksteal` (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:782`) each worker runs the
session-scoped fixture independently, so several can race the same `tests/e2e/js/node_modules`.

## Approach

Charge provisioning to the build, not to a test, and make the in-fixture fallback bounded and
race-safe. This shape is chosen because it fixes both halves of the defect class in the place
each one lives: the unbounded subprocess is a code defect in the fixture, and the cold install
on the critical path is a build-ordering defect in the workflow.

Portability is the constraint that rules out a CI-only fix (blocking `project.portability`): the
provisioning must still work in a checkout with no CI provider. So the primary path is a plain
`make e2e-deps` target that any developer or any CI system can invoke, and the fixture keeps
provisioning as a fallback — now with explicit `timeout=` values and a file lock — rather than
being deleted.

Extract the provisioning into `tests/e2e/_toolchain.py` (a small module beside the fixture, so
it is directly callable from a test without spawning pytest); `tests/e2e/conftest.py` calls it
and converts its error into the existing self-skip. A `fcntl.flock` on a lock file in
`tests/e2e/js/` serializes concurrent xdist workers, degrading to no lock where `fcntl` is
absent (single-process correctness is unaffected).

## Scope

- `tests/e2e/_toolchain.py` (new) — `provision_toolchain()` with explicit per-step `timeout=`,
  a step-naming `ToolchainProvisioningError`, and the cross-process lock.
- `tests/e2e/conftest.py` — `bpmn_harness` delegates to it and self-skips with the named message.
- `tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py` (new) — the tests below.
- `Makefile` — `e2e-deps` target: `npm ci` + `npm run build` in `tests/e2e/js`.
- `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` — an npm cache keyed on
  `tests/e2e/js/package-lock.json` plus a `make e2e-deps` step before the pytest step at
  `:781`.

## Testing

A stub `npm` on `PATH` (a shell script that sleeps, or that succeeds then sleeps) makes every
case deterministic and fast; no network and no real Node install is involved.

- Happy path: `provision_toolchain` against a stub `npm` that exits 0 returns without error and
  the build step runs.
- Failure path (the one that reproduces the bug): a stub `npm` that stalls past the explicit
  `timeout=` makes `provision_toolchain` raise within the bound, with a message naming the
  step — `npm install` for the install stall, `npm run build` for the build stall — instead of
  running unbounded into the 300s pytest budget.
- Concurrency path: two independent processes call `provision_toolchain` on the same directory
  at once against a stub `npm` that records enter/exit; their install spans do not overlap.
- Build-ordering: assert the Makefile exposes `e2e-deps` and that the workflow invokes it in a
  step preceding the pytest step, and caches on `tests/e2e/js/package-lock.json`.

Run with `pytest tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py -q`, plus `make lint` and
`make typecheck`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Both provisioning subprocesses carry an explicit `timeout=`, and exceeding one raises an
      error whose message names the provisioning step (`npm install` / `npm run build`) — never
      a worker kill and never a bare `node down`. Checked by
      `pytest tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py -q`, whose stalled-`npm` cases assert the
      call returns within the bound with the step named.
- [x] Toolchain provisioning is available as a portable pre-pytest step that needs no CI
      provider, and the in-fixture path still provisions in a checkout that never ran it.
      Checked by running `make e2e-deps` from a clean worktree, and by the fixture test that
      provisions from an empty directory with a stub `npm`.
- [x] CI caches the npm store keyed on `tests/e2e/js/package-lock.json` and provisions with
      `npm ci` rather than `npm install`. Checked by the workflow/Makefile assertions in
      `tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py` and by `make lint` (actionlint).
- [x] Concurrent provisioning by two or more xdist workers is serialized. Checked by the
      two-process test asserting non-overlapping install spans.
- [x] Verified in real time, not by waiting for a recurrence: with `tests/e2e/js/node_modules`
      and `tests/e2e/js/dist` removed, `make e2e-deps` followed by
      `pytest tests/e2e -n 4 --dist worksteal -q` completes with no worker kill and no
      `node down`, and the stalled-`npm` cases above show the diagnosable named failure instead.
      Both complete in one session.
